subject: Actuation MAP: acceptance tests, exit gates & contingency ladder
thread_body:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Actuation MAP: acceptance tests, exit gates & contingency ladder

Alex — attaching a draft MAP and a short acceptance-tests summary to align on what "done" looks for your pilot. High level asks:
- Confirm the three success KPIs in the sheet (latency P95, average token cost, and accuracy on the sample eval set).
- Agree on the go/no-go exit gates for the pilot cutover week and the contingency ladder if any gate fails.
- Confirm procurement timeline for the Dedicated slot in week-of-2027-01-11 so we can schedule the canary.

I put action owners in the MAP (column H) and two fallback paths: 1) scale-back to a smaller quantized profile and 2) temporary read-through routing to our hosted cluster. If either fallback is required we will treat it as a formal regression and run the post-mortem with your engineering leads.

Attachments: 20261129_MAP_draft_v1.xlsx (MAP matrix), acceptance-tests-summary.md (test definitions), nimble-sla-exception-request.pdf (optional request if you need a lower latency SLA during pilot).

Thanks — Vivek
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

— Reply —
From: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@nimblehealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@nimblehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Actuation MAP: acceptance tests, exit gates & contingency ladder

Vivek — thanks for this. A few quick clarifications from our side:
1) The "accuracy on sample eval set" — can you call out pass/fail thresholds? We need a deterministic definition for our compliance team.
2) For the fallback 'hosted cluster' path, what are the expected delta-cost and latency uplift? We need rough order-of-magnitude numbers to model budget impact.
3) Procurement is fine with the timeline but needs a single consolidated DocuSign when we agree final terms.

I'll loop in our engineering manager if we need deeper technical detail.

— Alex
Director, Product Engineering
NimbleHealth

On Tue, 30 Nov 2026 14:20:00 -0800 Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks Alex — answers inline and updated the acceptance-tests-summary.md (attached).
>
> 1) Accuracy thresholds: pass = >= 92% on the curated eval set (A/B tolerance 0.5 points). Fail = < 90%. Between 90–92% is a gray zone that triggers quality review and potential parameter tuning. We called this out in the MAP under "quality gate".
>
> 2) Hosted fallback impact: expect ~1.7x token cost and a median latency uplift of +80–120ms for typical queries (we've included a per-route sample in the MAP workbook). If you need the exact cost delta by route we can export the per-token delta.
>
> 3) DocuSign: understood — we'll prepare the purchase addendum once technical gates are green.
>
> I've added Marissa to own the test-run schedule and Ben to own rollback & metrics instrumentation. Lauren will own the procurement handoff.
>
> Vivek
> Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
>
> On Wed, 1 Dec 2026 08:03:00 -0800 Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> > Team / Alex — quick internal note and proposal for the contingency ladder so the MAP is actionable during the cutover week. Pasting the ladder here for visibility and tagging owners:
> >
> > Contingency ladder (cutover week):
> > - Level 0 (ideal): All KPIs green — proceed to staged ramp to Dedicated pool on day+2. Owner: Marissa.
> > - Level 1 (minor infra regression): P95 latency breach < 20% above SLA or accuracy in gray zone. Action: enable prefix KV caching for known prefixes + temporary batching increase (target: drop P95 by ~15%). Owner: Ben.
> > - Level 2 (quality regression): accuracy < 90% but no data leakage. Action: switch to the conservative quantized model variant and pause non-essential routes. Run immediate eval on narrowed prompt set. Owner: Vivek/Customer Eng.
> > - Level 3 (severe / compliance concern): any data-handling or privacy exception. Action: execute rollback to pre-pilot traffic split (100% to preexisting inference path), notify legal & security, and pause all writes. Owner: Lauren.
> >
> > I've also added a 2-hour 'failure window' SLA in the MAP: if we hit Level 2 or 3, the decked contingency steps must be executed within 2 hours and then a joint triage within 4 hours. That window comes from our internal ops playbook.
> >
> > Alex — please confirm these owners or suggest alternates on your side. If Procurement needs an SLA exception for the 2-hour failure window we can include that in the addendum (attached nimble-sla-exception-request.pdf).
> >
> > Marissa
> > Senior Solutions Architect
> > Redwood Inference
> >
> > On Wed, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800 Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@nimblehealth.com> wrote:
> > > Marissa / Vivek — this ladder looks good and clear. A few requests from our engineering manager (cc'd in this reply):
> > > - Can you add a short smoke-test script (100 queries across the 5 representative routes) and the exact metric extraction steps so our SRE can run it autonomously?
> > > - In Level 1, please quantify expected P95 after prefix caching (you mentioned ~15% drop — is that conservative?).
> > > - We'll sign the addendum for the 2-hour window but need confirmation that fallbacks won't trigger billable overages for routes under the temporary hosted fallback for the first 24 hours.
> > >
> > > I'll return with SRE contact details by EOD.
> > >
> > > — Alex
> > >
> > > On Thu, 2 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800 Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai> wrote:
> > > > Alex / Team — adding the smoke-test script inline and a conservative P95 expectation:
> > > >
> > > > Smoke script (high-level):
> > > > - 100 synthetic queries across 5 routes (20 each) mirroring 80/20 long/short prompt mix.
> > > > - Capture per-request latency, token counts, and model confidence score.
> > > > - Pass condition: P95 latency <= defined SLA * 1.20 and accuracy >= 92% on the sampled eval set.
> > > > - If accuracy in gray zone (90–92%) run focused prompt-rewrite cycles (10 iterations) and re-run smoke.
> > > >
> > > > Expected P95 after prefix KV caching: historically we've seen 10–18% P95 reduction depending on prefix reuse. Use 12% as conservative prior for planning (I've added this to the MAP workbook).
> > > >
> > > > Cost note: hosted fallback for 24h will be billed at hosted rates; we can add a one-time credit if this path is used during the pilot (I added a placeholder in the addendum for a "fallback credit"). Procurement: we'll surface this in the DocuSign addendum.
> > > >
> > > > Ben
> > > > Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference
> > >
> > > On Thu, 2 Dec 2026 15:27:00 -0800 Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai> wrote:
> > > > > Alex / Procurement — quick: once we lock KPI thresholds and the contingency ladder Alex confirmed, we'll prepare the single DocuSign packet (MAP + SLA addendum + PO reference). Please confirm the billing contact and PO number to reference.
> > > > >
> > > > > Alex Moreno replied with PO number later this afternoon (not shown) and procurement confirmed they will sign the DocuSign once we add the smoke script to the MAP and append the credit clause for hosted fallback under 24h.
> > > > >
> > > > > Final note: next steps captured in the MAP workbook (column I):
> > > > > - Marissa: schedule smoke run with Nimble SRE (target: 2026-12-08).
> > > > > - Ben: finalize KV caching config and pre-provision test tokens (target: 2026-12-04).
> > > > > - Lauren: prepare DocuSign (include fallback credit clause) (target: 2026-12-05).
> > > > > - Vivek: coordinate on call for acceptance sign-off after smoke (target: 2026-12-09).
> > > > >
> > > > > Thanks — all, good momentum.
> > > > >
> > > > > Lauren Bishop
> > > > > Director, Strategic Accounts
> > > > > Redwood Inference
